claims.text: The initial NiCoCrAl-based MPEA is a fully miscible, near-equiatomic solid solution with a conventional microstructure.
A lamellar microstructure lowers the critical Al concentration required to form a protective Al2O3 scale.
Y and Hf additions enhance lattice distortion in the substrate.
Dopant-enhanced lattice distortion raises vacancy formation energy in the Al-depletion zone.
Dopant-enhanced lattice distortion raises the migration barrier for Al.
The lamellar microstructure and lattice distortion jointly control the initial selective oxidation of Al.
Selective oxidation of Al promotes formation of a thermodynamically stable Al2O3 scale.
A dense, continuous, adherent protective scale suppresses inward oxygen diffusion and outward metal-cation transport, thereby slowing oxidation and preventing premature scale failure.
Combining a lamellar microstructure with lattice-distortion-induced diffusion suppression rapidly produces an exclusive, continuous Al2O3 scale.
The enhanced lattice distortion suppresses upward Al diffusion from the substrate.
Suppressing Al diffusion from the substrate limits sustained thermally grown oxide growth.
Reducing thermally grown oxide growth mitigates oxide-scale spallation and preserves material integrity.
The engineered alloy will have approximately a 50–60% lower TGO growth rate than the conventional NiCoCrAl baseline.
The engineered alloy will exhibit minimal or no scale spallation after prolonged oxidation at 1200 °C.
The proposed mechanism should operate under oxidizing conditions from approximately 1100 to 1200 °C.
The relative benefits of the proposed mechanism should be less pronounced at lower temperatures or in non-oxidizing environments.
